title: Bank-first log-depth collimation at depth ceil(84 log2 n): adaptive tolerance (21 log2 n)/(64 n^85), work O(n^89 L^3 2^(n/(84L))), O(n^87) qubits

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and fixed secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), L=max(1,log2 n), the SAME algorithm RB of proof.md (bank-first robust collimation with depth rule ell = ceil(84 log2 n) (the least integer with 2^ell >= n^84) for n >= 4096 and ell = 3 below, width 2^R0 with R0 = max(ceil(n/ell)+v, 2v+2), parameters computed from N as in proof.md Section 1) acquires exactly Qbank copies and outputs s with unconditional probability greater than 0.99 for every adversary of the adaptive malformed-copy model of proof.md Section 0 with epsilon(n) = \frac{21 \log_2 n}{64 n^{85}}, including the adversary that corrupts nothing. All four resource bounds hold jointly on EVERY execution branch, including failed merges, rejected copies, discarded trees, retries and aborts (hard caps, proof.md Section 9). Total charged sequential work T is O(n^89 L^3 2^(n/(84L))); growth index of the declared envelope 1.

For every N>=2 and fixed secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), L=max(1,log2 n), the SAME algorithm RB of proof.md (bank-first robust collimation with depth rule ell = ceil(84 log2 n) (the least integer with 2^ell >= n^84) for n >= 4096 and ell = 3 below, width 2^R0 with R0 = max(ceil(n/ell)+v, 2v+2), parameters computed from N as in proof.md Section 1) acquires exactly Qbank copies and outputs s with unconditional probability greater than 0.99 for every adversary of the adaptive malformed-copy model of proof.md Section 0 with epsilon(n) = \frac{21 \log_2 n}{64 n^{85}}, including the adversary that corrupts nothing. All four resource bounds hold jointly on EVERY execution branch, including failed merges, rejected copies, discarded trees, retries and aborts (hard caps, proof.md Section 9). Peak classical bits S_C is O(n L^2 2^(n/(84L))); growth index of the declared envelope 1.

All four resource bounds hold jointly on EVERY execution branch, including failed merges, rejected copies, discarded trees, retries and aborts (hard caps, proof.md Section 9). Peak qubits S_Q is O(n^87) (the bank holds Qbank (n+1) qubits); growth index 0.

For every N>=2 and fixed secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2 N), L=max(1,log2 n), the SAME algorithm RB of proof.md (bank-first robust collimation with depth rule ell = ceil(84 log2 n) (the least integer with 2^ell >= n^84) for n >= 4096 and ell = 3 below, width 2^R0 with R0 = max(ceil(n/ell)+v, 2v+2), parameters computed from N as in proof.md Section 1) acquires exactly Qbank copies and outputs s with unconditional probability greater than 0.99 for every adversary of the adaptive malformed-copy model of proof.md Section 0 with epsilon(n) = \frac{21 \log_2 n}{64 n^{85}}, including the adversary that corrupts nothing. All four resource bounds hold jointly on EVERY execution branch, including failed merges, rejected copies, discarded trees, retries and aborts (hard caps, proof.md Section 9). Total acquired source copies Q equals Qbank = O(n^86); growth index 0.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, put n = ceil(log2 N). The single bank-first algorithm RB of proof.md (depth rule ell = ceil(84 log2 n) (the least integer with 2^ell >= n^84) for n >= 4096 and ell = 3 below, parameters of Section 1) acquires exactly Qbank copies; at most floor(epsilon(n) Qbank) of them may be malformed under exactly the adaptive malformed-copy model in error_model, with epsilon(n) = \frac{21 \log_2 n}{64 n^{85}} for every N >= 2 and no validity threshold (the expression is 0 at n = 1, where no malformed copy is allowed). For every adversary of that model, including the one that corrupts nothing, the whole s is recovered with unconditional probability greater than 0.99, jointly with all four worst-case resource bounds of this same algorithm and configuration (proof.md: Lemma BF and Section 2, Section 7, and the failure budget of Section 9). This is a guaranteed fraction among acquired copies, not a per-copy probability.

structured.error_model: Adaptive malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm, and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an arbitrary (n+1)-qubit state (the register shape of an ideal copy) supplied from the adversary's system: it may be pure or mixed, may be entangled with the adversary's remaining system and with other malformed copies, and may depend on all of the information above; it is not entangled with clean copies or with the algorithm's workspace, ancillas or internal random bits. Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace), i.e. clean copies are independent ideal coset states. The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies; after delivery it has no access to the copy or to the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
